## Speed
How fast each measured model runs, against the previous release, is in the table on the [release page](https://github.com/aosama/astronomical/releases/tag/v0.2.136).
## What's new
- **One engine for every text model.** Models that fit in memory and models read partly from the SSD now run through the same engine, so a model no longer reloads when its memory picture changes. - **Change Maximum model RAM while a reply is being written.** A raise takes effect straight away. A lower that the reply cannot fit under is refused at once with the memory it needs, and the control turns red. Image generation and decision-model training still apply a change once they finish. - **Lowering the memory limit keeps each layer's most-used experts,** so a smaller limit no longer leaves parts of a model to be read from the SSD for every word. - **Ternary Bonsai 2.5, with vision and its draft model.** Prism packs now run on the shared engine with vision and drafting, and the Bonsai 2 entries are corrected. - **Neural Engine prompt reading** now works on the shared engine.
## Fixes
- After a settings reload refused a memory limit, every later change of the limit was refused until Astronomical restarted. That no longer happens. - The Ternary Bonsai 2 entry with a draft model no longer promises drafting it did not do. - The update window no longer shows a speed table it cannot display.
## For developers
- `PUT /v1/config/maximum-mlx-memory` answers `200` when the change is applied, including during a reply, and `400` with the reason when it is refused. It no longer answers `202` or `409`. - `/v1/status` no longer has `pending_mlx_memory_ceiling_bytes`, and its `configuration.memory` no longer has `pending_maximum_bytes`.
## Compatibility
Your settings, models and conversations carry over unchanged. Astronomical needs macOS 14.0 or later on Apple silicon.
The app is signed with a Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and delivered through a signed Sparkle update.
